newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to buy back 600,000 of its shares.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to buy back 600,000 of its shares.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Wednesday that it would buy back up to 600,000 of its shares worth up to 2.3 billion yen in order to introduce a stock option scheme for its employees.
The latest repurchase plan is separate from another plan announced last month to buy back up to 100 billion yen worth of its own shares.

Toyota also said that the number of the shares repurchased in the scheme announced last month would be 27 million at most. Toyota would repurchase these shares to use up profits and reduce the number of its outstanding shares.
The two legs of the share repurchase plan need to be approved by an annual shareholders' meeting on June 26.

In the stock option scheme, the company will offer the options to all 56 directors as of the end of the shareholders' meeting. Each will receive no more than 15,000 shares and no fewer than 5,000 shares.
The term of the scheme would be four years, Toyota said.
Stock options give holders the right to buy shares at a set price within a certain period.
Japan changed its law last Friday to allow firms to buy back up to 10 percent of their own shares for use in stock option schemes for employees and executives.
Orix Corp said on Wednesday it would buy back 168,000 shares worth 1.5 billion yen in order to introduce a stock option scheme for its employees.
Fujitsu Ltd said last Friday that it was also considering introducing a stock option programme as early as fiscal 1998/99, which starts in April 1998.
Nissan Motor has said it will decide whether to introduce a stock option scheme after checking the details of the revision of the law covering stock options.
